about.title: Artesia Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and the last thing a grieving family should have to navigate alone is a legal claim. Artesia sees dozens of injury collisions each year along corridors like Pioneer Boulevard, SR-91, and South Street, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. When a collision proves fatal, California law gives certain family members the right to bring a wrongful death action separate from any criminal case tied to the crash. We handle wrongful death claims for families in Artesia who have lost someone in a traffic collision. We understand the timelines, evidence, and documentation these claims require. There's no cost to speak with us, no obligation to proceed, and we work on contingency, meaning we're paid only if there's a recovery. You focus on your family; let us look at the legal side.
commonInjuries: Pedestrian struck at a marked or unmarked crosswalk
Motorcycle or bicycle crashes involving passenger vehicles
Multi-vehicle chain-reaction crashes during peak traffic hours

whyChoose.title: What Families in Artesia Should Know

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts who may file a wrongful death claim, giving priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We can help clarify who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts at the Date of Death
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity — such as a public road authority — carry a much shorter deadline. Because Artesia's busiest corridors include state and local roads, identifying the responsible party early matters.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the family has suffered. These are separate from any criminal proceedings and are decided in civil court.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Artesia?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a county or city road authority, may share responsibility for the crash, the deadline to act is much shorter. Speaking with us early helps preserve your family's options.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this type of claim?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under certain circumstances. We can review your family's situation and explain who has standing.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a state route like SR-91 instead of a city street?
items.answer: It can affect which agency or party may be responsible and what deadlines apply, since claims involving government entities carry shorter filing windows than claims against private drivers. Artesia's crash-prone corridors include both state highways and local streets, so identifying the correct responsible party matters. This is exactly the kind of detail we can sort out early in the process.

items.question: Is there any cost to talk with an attorney?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for an initial consultation. We work on contingency, meaning we are paid only if your family recovers compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
